description:
In this episode of 3ABN Today Bible Q&A, the panel tackles some of Scripture’s most thought-provoking and practical questions. From David and Goliath and the meaning of “Let us make man,” to prophecy, the Sabbath, and so-called “lost books” of the Bible, discover clear, biblical insights. The discussion also explores real-life issues, like making decisions, dealing with tradition, and living out your faith daily. Join us for honest answers that bring clarity, encouragement, and a deeper understanding of God’s Word.



Send us your Bible Questions! 
By email: BibleQA@3abn.org


1. Why was David’s killing of Goliath acceptable if God forbids murder? Was David being used by God? Still, how is this right?  

2. Who is God talking to in Genesis 1:26 when he says, “Let us make man in our image”? 

3. Does God fulfill some prophecies in ways we can’t see or hear—and is 1844 one of them? 

4. As a Christian who is strongly against pork eating, is it ok to prepare it for someone else if I'm required to do so? Is it okay for a Christian to prepare pork for others?

5. Although studying the Bible is essential, why is spending so much time studying prophecy like Daniel & Revelation so extremely important? I mean, God's going to do what He's going to do. If God’s plan is set, why study prophecy?

6. Can you please explain Jeremiah 3:16? 

7. If you ask God for something, receive it, lose it, and then it returns, but you no longer want it, what should you do? If you lose something God once gave, and He gives it back, but now it's unwanted, what do you do?

8. I have been a greeter in my church for many years and consider myself to be a self-appointed jester. As a greeter, I often see people who look sad, and I’ve made it my goal to try to bring a smile or even a little chuckle to their lives. Should I instead be more quiet and simply wish them a happy Sabbath? As a greeter, should I stay quiet instead of trying to make people smile?

9. Where can I find reliable information showing that the so-called “lost” or omitted books of the Bible were not actually lost or removed? Where can I find proof that the so-called “lost” books of the Bible were not lost?

10. When a Christian has a loving heart but resists studying biblical truth and clings to tradition, how can they be helped to see what the Bible really says? How can a Christian move beyond tradition and see biblical truth?

11. What exactly did God create on the first day? Also, why did he divide the day from the night and create day and night twice? Once on day 1 and once on day 4?

12. According to Mark 12:25, there won't be marriage after the resurrection. But according to Isaiah 65:23, people will have children on the new earth. If there's no marriage, how are people going to have children? Do Mark 12:25 and Isaiah 65:23 seem to contradict each other?
